title: Lehman Brothers is independent again
what: American Express has completed the spin-off of Lehman Brothers, the Wall Street bond trading and investment banking house founded in 1850 that it bought in 1984. Lehman, led since April by Richard Fuld, now trades on its own on the New York Stock Exchange. The firm lost $102 million in 1993.
why: Listing beat. A cheap, unloved bond house; from here Fuld would post fourteen straight years of profits before the collapse.

title: Lehman cuts costs after a hard first year
what: Lehman Brothers announced a programme of cost cuts at the end of its first year as an independent firm; it employed about 8,500 people. It has also moved its financial year to end in November.
why: The lean years: the stock went sideways until 1996. Headcount fell to about 7,800 in 1995.

title: Record year for Lehman
what: Lehman Brothers earned a record $647 million in the year to November 1997, or $4.72 a share, in a year of near-record underwriting volumes and mergers on Wall Street.
why: The shares rose about 60% in 1997, and Lehman was a full investment bank again, built on bond trading.
source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/806085/0000806085-99-000002.txt (Lehman press release, 7 January 1999, giving the 1997 figures; read 2026-10-03); https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/806085/0001047469-99-007702.txt (10-K fiscal 1998; read 2026-10-03)

title: Third rate cut; Wall Street recovers
what: The Federal Reserve has now cut interest rates three times since the end of September, and central banks in Europe have followed. Stocks have recovered most of the summer's losses, and the market for new share issues has reopened. Lehman's shares rose another third in November.
why: The recovery of autumn 1998 taught Wall Street that the Fed would step in during a panic, a lesson that encouraged risk-taking in the years before 2008.
source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/806085/0001047469-99-007702.txt (Lehman 10-K fiscal 1998: three Fed cuts, S&P 500 up 22% from 31 August to 30 November; read 2026-10-03)

title: Record 1998 for Lehman despite the autumn scare
what: Lehman Brothers reported record net income of $736 million for the year to November 1998, up 14%, or $5.19 a share, although fourth-quarter profit fell to $74 million from $185 million. 'Lehman Brothers achieved higher revenues and earnings in 1998 than in any other year in the firm's history,' said chief executive Richard Fuld.
why: The panic had been about survival; the results showed the firm had come through, and the shares kept recovering.

title: Lehman's quarterly profit more than doubles
what: Lehman Brothers earned a record $541 million in the quarter to February, up 156% from a year earlier, on record revenues of $2.2 billion, driven by share underwriting and merger advice in the technology boom. 'The firm is clearly hitting on all cylinders,' said Richard Fuld.
why: Boom-time earnings. The shares gained a third in March, a month in which the S&P 500 rose 10%. (Time check: 'at the height of' was a later verdict.)

title: Lehman buys Neuberger Berman for $2.6 billion
what: Lehman Brothers agreed to buy the fund manager Neuberger Berman for about $2.6 billion in cash and Lehman shares. The deal takes the assets Lehman manages for clients to more than $100 billion and makes it a leading firm for wealthy private investors.
why: Fuld's push to diversify away from trading; in September 2008 Lehman tried to sell this business to raise cash.

title: Lehman's profit jumps 39% to a record
what: Lehman Brothers' net income rose 39% to a record $2.4 billion in the year to November 2004, with a sixth consecutive year of record revenues from bond trading.
why: The mortgage boom years: Lehman was one of the biggest lenders and packagers of home loans, through its Aurora and BNC units.

title: Third record year in a row: $4 billion profit
what: Lehman Brothers earned a record $4.0 billion in the year to November 2006, up 23%, or $6.81 a share, its third consecutive year of record revenues and profits, with a pre-tax margin of 33.6%. Institutional Investor magazine named Richard Fuld the top chief executive among brokers and asset managers.
why: Peak confidence. Lehman's leverage, assets against equity, had risen from about 24 to 31 times by 2007.

title: Lehman joins a $22 billion apartment buyout
what: Lehman Brothers and the property firm Tishman Speyer agreed to buy Archstone-Smith, an owner of about 87,700 apartments in 359 communities, in a $22.2 billion deal.
why: A commercial property bet that Lehman could not sell on when credit dried up; it was a large part of the real-estate exposure that markets distrusted in 2008. (Time check: cut 'at the top of the property market', known only later.)

title: Another record quarter for Lehman
what: Lehman Brothers reported record net income of $1.3 billion for the quarter to May, up 27%, or $2.21 a share, and a record $2.4 billion for the half-year.
why: The last record. Within weeks the subprime mortgage market was breaking up, and Lehman closed its subprime lender in August.

title: Lehman shuts its subprime mortgage lender
what: Lehman Brothers is closing BNC Mortgage, its subprime home loan unit, cutting about 1,200 jobs in 23 locations, because market conditions 'necessitated a substantial reduction in its resources and capacity in the subprime space'. It will keep making mortgages through Aurora Loan Services. The shares fell 17% in July and another 12% in August.
why: The mortgage machine that drove the record profits was now losing money; the loans and securities Lehman still held were the problem.

title: Lehman reports a fourth record year as rivals write off billions
what: Lehman Brothers earned a record $4.2 billion in the year to November 2007, despite about $830 million of negative valuation adjustments in its bond business in the fourth quarter. Erin Callan has become chief financial officer.
why: While Citigroup was writing down billions, Lehman kept reporting profits, which later looked like reluctance to mark its holdings to market.

title: Bear Stearns falls, and fears turn to Lehman
what: Bear Stearns, the smallest of the big Wall Street firms, ran out of cash and was sold to JPMorgan Chase for $2 a share with Federal Reserve support on 16 March; analysts named Lehman as the next firm at risk. Lehman answered on 18 March with a first-quarter profit of $489 million and a cash reserve of $34 billion at the parent company, and its shares jumped 46% that day. They still ended the month down by a quarter.
why: The dress rehearsal. The market had learned that a firm can fail in days when its lenders pull back; Lehman's profit report bought time but not trust. (Time check: title 'Lehman is next in line' foreshadowed the failure.)

title: Lehman raises $4 billion
what: Lehman Brothers raised $4 billion of new capital by selling convertible preferred shares. Its shares recovered part of their March losses.
why: Raising money calmed investors for a few weeks; each new raise also told the market that Lehman needed it.
source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/806085/000110465908038647/a08-16256_1ex99d1.htm (Lehman press release, 9 June 2008, reporting the April issue; read 2026-10-03)

title: Hedge fund manager attacks Lehman's accounting
what: David Einhorn of Greenlight Capital, who said in April that he is betting against Lehman's shares, publicly questioned the firm's accounting for its real-estate holdings after a call with finance chief Erin Callan. Lehman's shares fell 17% in May.
why: A short-seller doing what the auditors did not. Lehman blamed short-sellers for its troubles; the losses announced in June showed Einhorn's doubts were justified.

title: Lehman's first loss: $2.8 billion; president and finance chief out
what: Lehman Brothers announced on 9 June its first quarterly loss as a public company, about $2.8 billion, as mortgage and real-estate holdings fell in value and some hedges failed, and said it was raising $6 billion of new capital. It said it had cut its leverage from 31.7 times its equity to under 25. On 12 June president Joseph Gregory and finance chief Erin Callan were replaced. The shares fell 46% in the month.
why: The point of no return: the losses were real, the capital raised was diluting, and the people Fuld had backed were gone.
source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/806085/000110465908038647/a08-16256_1ex99d1.htm (Lehman press release, 9 June 2008; read 2026-10-03); https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/806085/000110465908040477/a08-15739_16ex99d1.htm (12 June 2008; read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lehman_Brothers (read 2026-10-03)

title: Lehman Brothers files for bankruptcy
what: After talks with Bank of America and Barclays failed over the weekend and the government refused to back a rescue, Lehman Brothers filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on 15 September, with $639 billion of assets and debts of $613 billion to banks, the largest bankruptcy in U.S. history. The shares fell more than 90% that day and were removed from the New York Stock Exchange; the Dow Jones fell more than 500 points. Barclays agreed to buy Lehman's North American business for a fraction of its former value.
why: The exit, and the event that turned a credit crunch into a global panic. For the game's lesson: a firm with 30 times leverage, short-term funding and assets nobody trusts can go from record profits to zero in nine months.
